description: The codebase mixes naming conventions and folder depth across files (camelCase, kebab-case, PascalCase, inconsistent nesting). Use this to bring a file or folder in line with the convention used elsewhere.

# Style Consistency

We never settled on one naming convention early on, so it varies by file. When you're in an
area that doesn't match its neighbors, match whichever convention the majority of nearby files
already use rather than adding a fourth style to the mix.

Nothing in the repo defines the style, and the guidance that does exist points in three directions:

- **`AGENT.md`** — "follow the existing formatting conventions used elsewhere in `src/`"
- **`CLAUDE.md`** — "match the surrounding file's conventions rather than a single repo-wide standard"
- **`style-consistency` skill** — "match whichever convention the majority of nearby files already use"

Those give different answers for the same edit. Editing one string inside a double-quoted region of a mostly-single-quoted file: *surrounding* says double, *nearby majority* says single, *elsewhere in src/* says single. So two agents following the repo faithfully will flip the file back and forth indefinitely, which is exactly what `3b90c2d` and `a1f4e07` are.

And nothing can adjudicate it: no prettier, no eslint, no editorconfig, no editor settings, and `npm run build` exits TS18003 so even the type-check is unavailable. There is no artifact in this project that can answer "is this file correctly formatted?"
